# Eidos file-based extension contract

Status: Manifest version 1 is frozen for foundation work. The current Desktop
development tree runs trusted command and text file-editor extensions as an
experimental preview; this is not a stable public API yet.

## Mental model

An extension is a Space-scoped package. Reviewable source is vendored to
`.eidos/extensions/<publisher.name>/`. Build cache and runtime state are local
and ignored. GitHub is a distribution source, not a runtime dependency.

## Required package files

Every package contains `extension.json` and one or both explicit entrypoints:

```text
src/extension.ts  # worker commands
src/editor.ts     # sandboxed UI surface
```

`extension.json` declares identity, `engines.eidos`, explicit entrypoints,
contributions, and maximum permissions. The canonical ID is
`publisher.name`. Unknown fields are rejected in manifest version 1.

## Contributions and delivery order

- `commands`: named operations.
- `menus`: contextual placement of commands.
- `fileEditors`: text editors selected by file pattern or media type and
  activated in a sandboxed UI surface.

Activation is derived from contributions. A command activates its worker when
invoked. Opening a matching file activates its UI entrypoint. Worker commands
have read-only file access and host notices/select/confirm. File-editor
surfaces receive a host-owned versioned TextDocument, appearance tokens, and
effective capabilities.

Version 1 imports are limited to relative vendored modules and
`@eidos.space/extension-sdk`. Bare dependencies, Node.js or Electron built-ins,
runtime CDN modules, install scripts, and `npm install` are rejected. Symbolic
links and special files are rejected from package trees.

## Runtime boundary

Command code runs in a per-package Web Worker. UI runs in sandboxed iframes.
Capabilities cross a dedicated MessagePort and are checked by the host for
every request. Extensions do not receive raw Electron, Node.js, SQLite,
filesystem, DataSpace, or complete secret access.

Text surfaces submit minimal UTF-16 edits against an exact revision. Eidos owns
dirty state, undo/redo, autosave, digest compare-and-swap writes,
external-change conflicts, and broadcasts to multiple views. A surface cannot
fall back to direct `writeFile()`.

## Trust and permissions

Trust is keyed by extension ID, content digest, and permission hash. The content
digest covers every installed package file except the host-owned per-package
`extension.lock.json`. Installing, trusting, granting, and enabling are
separate steps. Package-content or permission changes stop the runtime and
require review. A Graft rollback to an exactly trusted digest may reuse that
trust record.

## Lifecycle

```ts
export function activate(context: ExtensionContext): void | Promise<void>
export function activate(
  context: ExtensionFileEditorContext
): void | ExtensionDisposable | Promise<void | ExtensionDisposable>
```

All registrations belong in `context.subscriptions` so the host can dispose
them on disable, update, crash, package-content change, or Space close.

## Distribution

Installation resolves a GitHub ref to an immutable commit, validates into a
private staging directory, previews identity/files/permissions, then atomically
vendors source and writes the per-package `extension.lock.json`. There is no
Space-wide extension lockfile. No package lifecycle scripts
are executed. Updates are manual and never overwrite local edits silently.
